_comment: Normative statements that an accepted decision has retired, and what replaced them.
scripts/check-retired-guidance.py fails when one appears as a live directive.
A line carrying a retired pattern is allowed when it also carries one of the
entry's `citation_markers` -- naming the superseding decision, or saying the
guidance is stale. That is the difference between DIRECTING against accepted
architecture and RECORDING that the old rule was retired, and only the first
is a defect. It also means the fix is never to delete the history: cite the
Add an entry whenever a decision supersedes normative text that is written
down somewhere else, so the retired phrasing cannot quietly outlive it.

entries.replacement: maistro-core carries the soft scope axes global -> org -> team -> user -> agent -> session; only the hard `tenant` boundary is Stronghold-specific. The retired shorthand conflated scope with tenancy.
